newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament approves minimum wage rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament approves minimum wage rise.

text.p: Russia's Federation Council upper house of parLiament on Wednesday approved a 10-percent rise in the minimum wage to 83,490 roubles from 75,900 roubles starting January 1, 1997.
President Boris Yeltsin must still sign the bill, which has been approved by both houses of parliament.
Yeltsin vowed to help solve the problem of low living standards in Russia on Wednesday.
Few Russians are paid the minimum wage, but it is important as a benchmark for calculating public sector pay, benefits, taxes and fines.
The minimum wage was last raised in April to 75,900 from 63,250 roubles.
Communist deputies often push to index the minimum wage to take inflation into account.
